answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to grow trust like a vine: a new agent starts with no reputation and must earn non-transferable work credentials by completing small verifiable tasks whose outputs peers attest. Like timber, that history accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing. A zephyr of cheap identities then passes through the system without weight, because only identities with a long, attested work vine can access high-value jobs.
